Q: What is a trusted source for a browser download?
Option1: The official vendor site or managed enterprise store
Option2: Any site returned by a search engine
Option3: A link in an unsolicited email

Q: Why verify file hashes for installers?
Option1: To confirm the download matches the vendor release and is not altered

Q: What is the risk of installing from untrusted sources?
Option1: Malware or unwanted add ons may be bundled

Q: What are extensions and plug ins?
Option1: Add on modules that extend browser features and can add risk

Q: What is the guidance for extension security?
Option1: Use only trusted and needed extensions and review permissions

Q: What is the purpose of a password manager in a browser?
Option1: Store and auto fill unique complex passwords securely
Option2: Share one password across all sites

Q: What does a valid certificate indicate when visiting a site?
Option1: That the connection is encrypted and the site identity was validated by a certificate authority
Option2: That the site is safe from all threats
Option3: That the site will never track users
Option4: That the site is government owned

Q: What does the padlock icon in the address bar indicate?
Option1: That Transport Layer Security is in use and the certificate is valid
Option4: That the site is trusted by your manager

Q: What is a pop up blocker for?
Option1: Prevent windows or tabs from opening without user action
Option2: Clear the browser cache on exit

Q: What does clearing browsing data do?
Option1: Removes history, cookies, and cached items to reduce tracking or fix issues

Q: What is the cache used for?
Option1: Stores copies of web resources to speed up page loads

Q: What is private browsing mode intended to do?
Option1: Limit local storage of history and cookies for that session
Option2: Provide end to end anonymity on the internet

Q: What is the function of sign in and browser data sync?
Option1: Sync bookmarks, passwords, history, and settings across devices
Option2: Provide multi factor authentication for all sites
Option3: Share browsing data with other users by default

Q: What is a risk of browser sync on shared or unmanaged devices?
Option1: Sensitive data such as passwords or history may be copied to devices you do not control
Option3: The device will not connect to wireless

Q: What is an ad blocker used for?
Option1: Reduce or block advertising content and some tracking scripts
Option3: Provide antivirus at the kernel level

Q: What is a good practice after installing a new browser?
Option1: Set security and privacy defaults, update, and sign in only on trusted devices
Option2: Disable automatic updates and install many extensions

Q: What should users check if a site shows a certificate warning?
Option1: Inspect the certificate details and avoid proceeding unless it is trusted and current

Q: What browser feature helps contain malicious tabs?
Option1: Site isolation or sandboxing

Q: What is the safest approach for built in document or media plug in handling?
Option1: Use built in viewers or trusted vendors and keep them updated
Option2: Install multiple third party viewers from forums
Option3: Disable all viewers and share files by email

Q: Which cookie setting reduces tracking without breaking logins as often?
Option1: Block third party cookies or use stricter tracking prevention
Option2: Block all cookies for all sites

Q: A user installed an untrusted extension then saw pop ups and redirects. What is the fix?
Option1: Remove the extension, scan for malware, reset settings, and review permissions
Option3: Lower the pop up blocker level

Q: Why is hashing important for offline installer packages?
Option1: It confirms integrity when not using a store that verifies downloads

Q: How can an administrator control extensions in a company?
Option1: Use policy to allow or block specific extensions and set permissions

Q: Which combination best hardens a browser for daily use?
Option1: Automatic updates on, limited trusted extensions, password manager, phishing and malware protection, and ad or script controls as needed
Option2: Disable updates, install many extensions, and allow all pop ups
Option3: Turn off certificate checks and block Transport Layer Security
Option4: Use public sync on every kiosk

Q: A site shows a certificate name mismatch. What should you do?
Option1: Do not proceed; verify the URL and certificate details with the site owner
Option2: Proceed because the lock icon is shown
Option3: Turn off the pop up blocker

Q: Which cookie setting reduces tracking with minimal breakage?
Option1: Block third party cookies or enable strict tracking prevention
Option2: Block all cookies for every site
